task: Implement safe priority structures whose exported records can be directly constructed while preserving the frozen malformed-state contract and documented complexity.
observation: The frozen API exposes directly constructible heap and priority-queue records, so a public operation cannot trust the heap-order or parallel-vector invariants. Rejecting forged malformed records requires a full O(n) validation before an otherwise O(log n) sift operation; Moss v0.1 provides no opaque exported-record boundary that would let constructors certify the invariant once.
impact: Public heap and priority-queue operations are O(n) including mandatory validation, even though bottom-up heapify remains O(n) and the mutation algorithms themselves are O(log n). The package documents this cost instead of making an inflated end-to-end complexity claim; deque operations remain O(1) because deque metadata validation is O(1).

resolution.summary: Every public operation validates first and raises DataStructureError.InvalidState for forged state. A future opaque-record facility could restore end-to-end O(log n) public heap operations without weakening malformed-input rejection.

suggestion: Provide an opaque exported record or private-field construction boundary so SDKs can maintain representation invariants without rescanning the full structure on each operation.
